name: Signal Values Live Fast Path

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Signal Values Live Fast Path Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

Every change delivered to a `Signal::values()` subscriber locks that subscription's startup mutex to decide between buffering (before the baseline is delivered) and forwarding, long after startup ended. Recording the live phase in an atomic flag and the last delivered version in an `AtomicU64` (`fetch_max`) forwards live changes without the mutex; the mutex is kept only for the buffering phase and the hand-over, so ordering and the never-older-after-newer rule are unchanged.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** atomic live-phase fast path for `values()` deliveries.
**Allowed changes:** `SignalInner::values` and its startup state in `crates/src/signal.rs`.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** DeliveryQueue changes, Computed changes, `changes()` stream.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Scalar tests (`tests`, `scalar_tests`), signal startup/race tests, full lib + integration tests; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` scalar-hot, `reactive_complexity`. Pass: `signal-set-one-subscriber` >=10% faster on rerun; `signal-and-computed/*` subscribe-heavy benches not slower >10%.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

~5-10 ns less per delivered value per subscriber.

## Signal Values Live Fast Path Finished

**Index:** 15
**Checkpoint:** 4a6b594
**Attempt Count:** 1

### Report

**Passed Status**: false — Reverted failure. The live-path mutex costs ~2-3 ns per delivery; not worth a subscription-setup regression.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** tests pass; steady-state delivery improved on rerun (signal-set-one-subscriber -11.6%, effect -12%; a first run showed +70%, bimodal scheduling noise), but the subscribe-per-iteration bench signal-and-computed/signal/1 regressed +20% and +22% on two runs (computed/1 +17%/+8%), failing the <10% gate.
**Out-of-scope changes:** none.
